text:
The Maple Leafs have not won in nine games (0-8-1), they have been outscored 37-18, and the chances say it is real: 44% of the expected goals over the skid (expected goals measure the quality of chances). Saturday was the worst version yet, a two-goal lead that turned into a 4-3 loss to Columbus. Auston Matthews called it "inexcusable," William Nylander called his giveaway on the tying goal a "dumb play," and a Daily Faceoff Toronto piece raised whether a ninth straight loss "may end Jim Hiller's tenure." Speculation about Matthews' future and Nylander's situation has filled the gaps between games.

In net, Sergei Bobrovsky has been part of it: .827 and 7.6 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, all losses. Kirill Marchenko, who has 14 points in 14 games since coming over from Columbus, is out; John Tavares has moved up beside Nick Paul and Nylander, and Easton Cowan is playing 20 minutes a night, which is why he is one of our Sleepers. Tavares also returns to the building of the team that drafted him first overall in 2009. Our numbers give Toronto a 2% playoff chance.

The Islanders have points in seven straight (4-0-3) and a +9 goal difference, but our numbers flag it: they have taken 47% of the expected goals, -7.9 on chances. Ilya Sorokin is doing the lifting, at 11.2 goals saved above expected this season and .928 over his last five. Matthew Schaefer has 15 points in his last ten and 25 on the season, including a hat trick against Columbus, and Simon Holmstrom carries a seven-game point streak (six goals). On Saturday in Detroit, Casey Cizikas played his 1,000th game and picked up an assist.

These teams met October 17, a 4-1 Islanders win. Tonight we have New York at 3.78 expected goals and Toronto at 2.68. For the Leafs the problem is both ends at once: a goalie who has given up 7.6 more than expected in five starts, facing one who has saved 5.6 more.
headline: Winless Leafs carry nine straight into Long Island
